# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the

MCP servers in your MCPJam projects: diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
>
**The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surfa
ce may change, including in\n> breaking ways, while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on t
his page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord]

(https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or
> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https:

//app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be aske

d to sign in and then land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hos

ted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects (from CI, scripts, or your own agents)
without opening the UI.

What

you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resources**: list your projects, their servers, eval
 suites, and chat sessions,
so every ID the other routes need is\n self-serve\n* **Validate a server**: connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapsho
t\n* **Run the doctor**: the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements**: does this serve
r need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources**: the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt**
: execute primitives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot**: tools, reso
urces, and prompts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients**: list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template lik
e `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that defi
ne how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId
